## ai.proxy: local CLIProxyAPI for AI harnesses

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-21 — root and per-runtime `url` or `instance`
> selections resolve to `{key; url;}`; a runtime routed through an instance gets
> its own key, allowlist entry and key claim there, and enables the instance's
> `providers` by name; Claude and Codex consume the key through credential
> helpers, and other runtimes warn.

`ai.proxy` points a harness at a locally hosted CLIProxyAPI so the harness holds
only the proxy's client key, never an upstream credential. The proxy holds the
logins. `ai.mcpServers.<name>.proxy` (lib/ai/mcpProxy.nix) is an unrelated MCP
credential proxy.

### Shape

- Library: `lib/ai/proxy/default.nix`. Options, validation and `resolve` live
  there.
- `sharedOptions.nix` registers the root option and asserts the root selection.
- `proxy` is a key of `sharedSurfaceOptions`, so it is a delivery-policy surface
  and every enabled runtime whose `surfaceSupport` omits `proxy` gets the
  standard decomposition warning. Claude and Codex declare support; the other
  runtimes warn rather than dropping a selection silently.
- `mkBackendTransform.nix`, for a record whose `surfaceSupport` declares
  `proxy`, declares `ai.<runtime>.proxy` (the root's selection options plus
  `allow` and `providers`) and `ai.<runtime>.normalized.proxy`. The callbacks
  get it as `normalized.proxy` and `resolvedProxy`. Inside the runtime's enable
  gate it publishes the runtime's client and key claim (below).

### Selection and the resolved endpoint

A selection is `url` + `key` for a proxy configured by hand, or `instance` +
`key` for one this flake runs. `instance` names an `ai.cliproxyapi.instances`
entry (`packages/cliproxyapi/modules/instances.nix`) and resolves through
`packages/ai-module/lib/instances.nix`'s `select` to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`;
`url` and `instance` are mutually exclusive. A selection without a key, a key
without a selection, or an instance that is missing or disabled fails as an
assertion at either scope, outside the runtime enable gate; such an instance
resolves to null. A selection without a key is rejected because the harness
would send its own login token, if any, to the proxy. The instances are read as
`config.ai.cliproxyapi.instances or {}`, since an evaluation without the owner
module (the factory harness) has none.

A per-runtime selection that selects anything (a `url` or an `instance`)
replaces the root selection WHOLE. Fields never mix across levels: a runtime
`key` alone leaves the root selection in force and fails its own assertion. The
resolved value is null or `{key; url;}`. `url` is the origin only: each runtime
appends its own protocol path, so a path would be doubled.

`key` requires `redact.types.redacted`: `redact.file`, `redact.command` or
`redact.concat` with a reference. It authenticates access to the proxy's
upstream subscriptions, so cleartext has no harmless use here. Root and
per-runtime options use the same type as the normalized endpoint.

References remain unresolved during evaluation. A consuming runtime must use
`redact.assign` when its launcher or credential helper starts and escape the
resolved value for its destination format. A key's contents cannot be
charset-checked at evaluation; never substitute the runtime value unescaped into
JSON, TOML or shell source. The `url` pattern validates only the proxy origin.

### Runtime keys and the allowlist

A runtime routed through an instance owns its client key there. The transform
publishes `proxyLib.client` — `{instance; key; allow; credentials; option;}` —
at `ai.internal.proxyClients.<runtime>`, and
`packages/cliproxyapi/modules/instances.nix` reads its instance's clients
(`clientsOf`) in the instance's derived settings: each key joins
`access.api-keys` and gets one `access.key-allowlist` entry whose `credentials`
are `allow` followed by one rule per enabled provider. CPA then fails closed for
every listed key (`cliproxyapi-key-allowlist.md`), so the key reaches only those
credentials. The launcher gets the same `key` through `normalized.proxy`, so the
published key and the presented key are one reference.

The instance pulls; the runtime never writes `ai.cliproxyapi.instances`. A
pushed definition would create the instance a typo names, hiding the "not an
entry" assertion, and checking existence from inside that definition recurses.
`ai.internal` is an option group, outside the root-pool provenance guard.

`allow` takes `access.key-allowlist[].credentials`'s generated type
(`cliproxyapi.keyAllowlistCredentialsType`), so a bad `kind` fails at the
runtime option. Its default is the record's `proxyAllow`: Claude's and Codex's
own OAuth login (`sdk/auth/{claude,codex}.go`, `Provider`). A runtime without
one has no default; an enabled runtime routed through an instance with neither
`allow` nor an enabled provider is refused. `allow` and `providers` are not part
of the selection: they apply whichever scope selects. `allow` stays as the
escape hatch for what providers cannot express: dropping the own login
(`allow = []`), narrowing it by `ids`, and reaching a hand-written block.

### Providers

`ai.cliproxyapi.instances.<n>.providers.<name>` is `{key; models; apis}`, with
`apis.{anthropic,chat,responses}.base-url`.
`packages/cliproxyapi/lib/providers.nix` holds the one API table: `anthropic` →
`api-keys.claude`, `responses` → `api-keys.codex` (key gets
`disable-codex-cloaking`), `chat` → `api-keys.openai-compatibility` named after
the provider. The instance's derived settings append those blocks to any written
by hand; the list type concatenates.

`ai.<runtime>.proxy.providers.<name> = {enable; api ? null;}`. `providersFor`
resolves each enabled one against the selection's instance; `api` null means the
record's `proxyApi` (Claude `anthropic`, Codex `responses`), declared in each
factory so this library stays provider-agnostic. The rule is
`{provider; kind = "apikey"; base-urls = [<that api's base-url>];}`, the string
the block got, because CPA matches base URLs exactly after trimming Go's
`strings.TrimSpace` (every Unicode space), which Nix's trim does not reproduce.
So a provider base URL must be printable ASCII (`https?://[!-~]+`), a
hand-written block in a provider's family must start and end with a printable
ASCII character, and no other block of the family may share a provider's URL:
with both URLs trim-free the exact comparison equals CPA's. A provider name must
be one plain word, since it becomes a group name and a credential provider.

Refused at evaluation, inside the enable gate:

- One key REFERENCE on two runtimes: each claims
  `proxy-client-key.<reference as JSON>` through `ai.<runtime>.claims`, so the
  claim registry fails. A root `instance` selection therefore serves one enabled
  runtime; another selects with its own key. The claim compares references, not
  resolved values. Two different references that resolve to one value (trimmed)
  pass evaluation and are refused by CPA instead, which fails closed: at start
  it logs the error naming the entries by index and never the key, and exits
  non-zero; on a hot reload it keeps the running config and allowlist. Operator
  decision 2026-10-21; `packages/cliproxyapi/docs/cliproxyapi-key-allowlist.md`.
- A runtime key also listed by hand in `access.api-keys`, or given a
  hand-written `access.key-allowlist` entry: a second owner could widen or
  contradict its rules. The count compares against the runtime clients with that
  key, so a shared key reports only the claim.

A `url` selection and a disabled runtime publish nothing. A hand-written key of
some other client stays allowed, but once any runtime routes through the
instance the allowlist is set, so that key needs its own hand-written entry.

### Checks

`checks/ai-proxy/module-eval.nix` covers selection validation, redacted key
refusal and the per-runtime override through a test runtime that declares
`proxy`, each with the instance case on both backends.
`module-ai-proxy-instance-clients` routes Claude and Codex through one instance
and holds every routing refusal in one table, `routingCases`;
`module-service-instances-runtime-providers` runs the packaged CPA on generated
config. The unsupported-runtime warnings are `ai-warnings-delivery`'s generated
cases, driven by its `proxy` sample (the url form).
`checks/ai-factory/factory-eval.nix` carries `proxy` in its every-surface
request set. `packages/claude-code/checks/claude-proxy.nix` checks settings and
runs the file, command and concat helpers on both backends.
`packages/chatgpt-codex/checks/chatgpt-codex-proxy.nix` checks Codex's provider
settings and session flags, runs the reference helpers, and sends requests
through the pinned Codex to loopback proxies on both backends.
